title: PRD and Launch Plan for Chat/Completions/Embeddings/Rerank API Primitives
creator: Ava Patel
overview: This PRD defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist for the initial shipment of Redwood's hosted API primitives: chat (conversational API), completions (single-turn generation), embeddings, and rerank. The goal is to provide a stable, documented, and observable surface that teams can adopt for production LLM features while preserving rollout flexibility and backward compatibility with existing beta customers.
background: Customers have requested a single predictable API for common inference primitives with clear SLAs, telemetry, and SDK parity. Engineering has delivered prototype runtime support for streaming, function calling hooks, and batched embeddings. This PRD consolidates product decisions, scope, trade-offs, and launch criteria for GA of these endpoints.
success_metrics: 99.9% successful API responses (5xx < 0.1%) within first 30 days
Average p95 latency for non-streaming completions <= 180ms for short prompts on dedicated capacity
Embedding throughput allows 1M tokens/day at predicted cost targets for three pilot customers
Adoption: 20 customers convert from beta to GA + 10 new integrating customers in first quarter
Telemetry coverage: token-level cost, per-model latency, and per-route error breakdowns instrumented
scope: IN: public REST endpoints for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank with SDK examples (Python/Node), streaming support for chat/completions, function-calling contract for chat, structured output hints, basic rate limiting and quotas, per-route observability dashboards, and a documented fallback policy for model variants. OUT: multi-region active-active routing, marketplace billing integrations, advanced rerank multi-pass algorithms, and on-prem private packaging (handled in a follow-up release).
goals: Ship stable API primitives with clear contracts and examples that teams can use for production features
Provide observability and cost signals that let customers estimate unit economics
Ensure predictable behavior under load with tested fallback and quota behaviors
Keep the launch footprint narrow enough to meet the release date but broad enough to unblock major customers
non_goals: Providing enterprise-only features like tenant-specific model pinning in this release
Full SDK parity for all language ecosystems beyond Python/Node
Delivering advanced optimizer suggestions (quant profiles) in GA
api_surface_summary: Four primary routes: /v1/chat (conversational streams + messages + function calling), /v1/completions (single-turn generation with streaming optional), /v1/embeddings (batched embedding creation with size hints), /v1/rerank (score list of candidates given query). Each route includes model, version, temperature/top_p controls where applicable, top-level metadata for request_id and billing tags, and an optional 'response_format' hint to request structured outputs.
functional_requirements: R1: Request/response JSON contract documented with examples for sync and streaming modes
R2: SDK examples for Python and Node including streaming handlers and retries
R3: Idempotency token support for safe retries on client side
R4: Server-side quota enforcement with clear error codes and Retry-After header
R5: Telemetry events emitted: request.received, response.sent, token.count, model.fallback, batch.size
R6: Model fallback policy configurable per-customer with documented priority rules
R7: Rerank returns per-item score and stable deterministic tie-breaker when models are non-deterministic
R8: Embeddings endpoint handles batching up to configured size; returns consistent vector dimensionality per model
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Endpoint 99.9% availability SLA for Dedicated customers; hosted API target 99.95% platform-wide uptime
NFR2: P95 latency targets published per-model in the catalog
NFR3: PCI/PII data controls: default no-retention mode and explicit retention flags
NFR4: Audit logs for admin actions and per-request KMS key usage recorded
acceptance_criteria: AC1: All four endpoints have full API docs, sample requests, and SDK snippets in the public docs site
AC2: E2E tests passing: functional, streaming, retry/idem, quotas, and fallback behavior in CI
AC3: Load test validates p95 latency at target throughput for baseline model on Dedicated pool
AC4: Telemetry shows request-level token counts, model selection, and error breakdowns for trial customers
AC5: Security review signed off and KMS integration tested with synthetic encryption/decryption
AC6: Runbook produced including rollback steps and thresholds for automatic rollback during canary
AC7: SDK package versions published and smoke-tested by integration test apps
quality_and_regressions: We will create a small eval suite with representative prompts (generation quality, hallucination checks, rerank correctness on curated datasets) and wire regression alerts into Console. Any model quality regression above configured thresholds will block release for that model variant.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal Canary): internal teams only, 48h monitoring with SLO watch and manual rollback
Phase 1 (Beta customers): 5 pilot customers with staggered traffic (10%, 30%, 100%) over 10 days with daily review
Phase 2 (Open GA): ramp to general availability with quota limits and optional invite gating for first week
Fallback policy: auto-fallback to compatible model variant when capacity or error rates cross thresholds
launch_checklist: Product: finalize API naming, deprecation policy, and user communications
Engineering: complete CI e2e tests, run load tests, and finish SDK publishing
Design: finalize example UX patterns for structured output and function calling in docs
Security: complete threat model review, KMS test, and SSO/roles audit
Compliance: confirm data retention controls and update DPA language
Telemetry: dashboards created for per-route latency/error/cost and alert rules configured
Support: runbook published, escalation contacts added, incident playbook rehearsed
Legal: TOS/usage policy updated for hosted inference
Go-to-market: release notes, migration guide for beta users, API versioning notes
test_plan: Unit & integration: cover request validation, response schema, and SDK behavior
Chaos tests: simulate worker failures and validate model fallback correctness
Load: sustained QPS at 2x expected for first 72h of GA with latency SLOs monitored
Security: run static scanning, dependency checks, and penetration test for endpoints
Model quality: run curated prompt suite and validate against baseline thresholds
scope_changes_and_tradeoffs: SCOPE REDUCTION #1: Postpone multi-region active-active support to next milestone to reduce ops complexity (decision: defer)
SCOPE REDUCTION #2: Limit SDK shipping to Python/Node for GA; other languages will be community-priority or next cycle
TRADEOFF: Streaming default vs. CPU cost — streaming enabled but with documented tradeoffs for high-concurrency scenarios
TRADEOFF: Rerank algorithm simplified to single-pass scoring for launch to achieve determinism and lower latency
open_questions: Q1: Do we expose a separate billing meter for rerank calls or include them in token-based billing? (Finance + Product decision needed)
Q2: Should the embeddings endpoint enforce a hard per-request vector count limit at the API layer or return a clear error recommending batching?
Q3: What default retention window for logs do we expose to self-serve customers before requiring support to change?
risk_mitigation: Risk: Early GA traffic spikes lead to latency SLO breaches. Mitigation: staged canary with automated rollback thresholds and capacity buffer
Risk: Customers misinterpret structured output hints and rely on them for parsing. Mitigation: docs with best practices and a structured-output validation tool in SDK
Risk: Model quality regression unnoticed. Mitigation: automated eval runs and regression alerts in Console before and after deployments
stakeholders: Eng Leads: Jonah Brooks, Mei Chen
communications: Pre-launch: targeted emails to beta customers, changelog entry, and API deprecation guide for any conflicting legacy routes. Launch-day: blog + docs + release notes + customer success outreach. Post-launch: weekly adoption dashboard and weekly incident reviews for first month.
decisions_log: D1: Use three separate endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings) rather than a single polymorphic endpoint to reduce client complexity
D2: Rerank returns normalized scores in range [0,1] and a stable tie-breaker hash
D3: Streaming implemented via SSE/WebSocket adapters; SDKs expose simple iterator/async iterator interfaces
notes: This PRD aims to be minimally prescriptive where engineering has a clear better approach (e.g., batching heuristics) and prescriptive elsewhere where customer contracts and observability are critical. Expect a follow-up PRD targeting Dedicated and Private deployment parity in Q2.
